title: Natural Grocers not worried about online grocery sales, still plans to open stores in 2017 (Photos)
summary: Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage plans to open eight new stores in five states by 2018, including a new store in Denver this month, despite current trends in online grocery sales and recent industry acquisitions. The Lakewood-based company is not worried about the shift to online grocery and continues its expansion.

title: O'Reilly Auto stock plummets: Down 19 percent Wednesday, lowest price since late 2014
summary: O'Reilly Automotive's stock plummeted 18.9 percent on Wednesday, reaching its lowest price since November 2014, after the company announced weaker-than-expected second-quarter sales results. Same-store sales rose only 1.7 percent against a forecast of 3 to 5 percent, with CEO Greg Henslee citing a mild winter and weak consumer demand. The news also negatively impacted competitors Advance Auto Parts and Autozone.

title: Campbell Just Spent $700 Million on a Soup Company
summary: Campbell Soup announced its acquisition of Pacific Foods for $700 million in cash, a strategic move to address evolving consumer preferences for natural and organic products. Pacific Foods, known for its organic broth, soup, and plant-based beverages, will help Campbell expand into faster-growing market segments. This acquisition is part of Campbell's broader strategy to adapt to a changing food industry landscape, marked by a shift away from processed foods and increased demand for organic options.

title: QVC Parent Scoops Up Rival HSN For $2.1 Billion
summary: Liberty Interactive, parent company of QVC, has acquired the remaining 61.8% stake in HSN Inc. for $2.1 billion, merging the two retail giants. The combined entity will become the third-largest e-Commerce company in North America by sales, behind Amazon.com and Walmart. This strategic move aims to enhance scale, reduce costs, optimize programming, and strengthen cross-marketing efforts.

title: QVC Parent to Buy HSN in $2.6B Deal
summary: Liberty Interactive Corp., parent company of QVC, is acquiring the remaining 61.8 percent stake in rival home shopping network HSN Inc. in a deal valued at $2.6 billion, making HSN a wholly owned subsidiary. The merger brings together two major players in the home shopping arena, collectively selling over $800 million in jewelry and watches annually, at a time when they are competing with online retailers. The all-stock transaction is expected to be completed by Q4 2017, and HSNi will become part of the newly formed QVC Group Inc. after Liberty Interactive spins off QVC and Zulily.

title: Why Entrepreneurs Should Feel Optimistic About the QVC-HSN Merger
summary: The merger of QVC and HSN, with Liberty Interactive acquiring HSN for $2.6 billion, presents a promising outlook for entrepreneurs selling products on these platforms. Experts and sellers believe the combined entity will offer greater scale, reach a wider customer base, and potentially open new sales channels for entrepreneurs who previously had to choose between the two companies. While both brands will remain separate, the consolidation is expected to benefit businesses seeking broader market access.

title: QVC-HSN merger puts Amazon and Walmart on notice
summary: The merger between QVC and HSN Inc. will create the No. 1 global video commerce company with $14 billion in revenue and position it as the No. 3 e-commerce and mobile commerce player behind Amazon and Walmart. This consolidation aims to leverage synergies and push into online sales, particularly mobile, presenting a significant competitive challenge to the e-commerce giants. Industry experts expect the merger to drive groundbreaking innovation in television-enabled commerce and novel shopping experiences.

title: Do Retailers Have an Answer to Amazon Prime Day?
summary: This article discusses Amazon's strategy for Prime Day, which focuses on gaining new Prime subscribers rather than just sales. It also examines how other online retailers are attempting to compete, primarily through extensive discounting, a strategy that has not been very successful in increasing sell-throughs. The piece highlights the significant advantage Amazon gains from its Prime membership program and how traditional retailers struggle to compete once consumers are subscribed.

title: Abercrombie & Fitch takes itself off the block
summary: Abercrombie & Fitch has announced it is no longer seeking a sale, disappointing investors hoping for a rescue of the struggling teen retailer. The decision led to a 21 percent plunge in shares to a 17-year low. The company plans to stick with its current strategy to improve performance, despite wider first-quarter losses and declining revenue.

title: Entrepreneurs prepare for Amazon Prime Day
summary: Small businesses like Surrey entrepreneur Oliver Bleicher's HappyGrün are preparing to participate in Amazon Prime Day, using the high-traffic event not just for sales but also for product exposure and customer reviews. While the event offers significant sales bumps and visibility to millions of shoppers, experts caution small businesses against solely relying on Amazon for revenue, advocating for a multi-channel sales approach. Analysts estimated that Amazon generated over US$500 million in sales on Prime Day in 2016, with expectations for the 2017 event to set new records due to increased Prime memberships and product offerings.

title: 9 American Businesses That Amazon and Jeff Bezos Will Never Target
summary: This article identifies nine American businesses that Amazon and Jeff Bezos are unlikely to target, offering insight into companies immune to Amazon's expansive reach. It details the criteria for immunity, including large market value, wide moats against competition, solid track records, global growth potential, and positive analyst target prices. The businesses span various sectors such as utilities, cruise lines, theme parks, entertainment, and waste management.

title: Cold-storage plant gets cold shoulder from neighbors, but ultimately wins approval
summary: A proposed 450,000-square-foot cold-storage facility for food, developed by Lineage Logistics, near Gardner, Kansas, has received unanimous approval from the county commission despite strong opposition from local neighbors. Residents voiced concerns about noise, lighting, and water runoff, citing unfulfilled promises and negative experiences with a previous tenant, Kimberly-Clark, which had also received a tax abatement. The neighbors' protest petition was declared invalid due to a technicality, and their request for a delayed vote to allow developer-resident dialogue was denied, leaving them disappointed with the commission's decision.

title: Five9 Takes on the World
summary: Five9 announced significant architectural changes to its Virtual Contact Center (VCC) application as part of its Summer Release 2017. These changes aim to enhance the platform for enterprise and global scalability, moving towards a microservices-based architecture and introducing new voice points of presence. The update also includes tighter integrations with WFO solutions from partners and with Salesforce and Microsoft Skype for Business, signaling Five9's intent to target the large enterprise contact center market.

title: Intel rolls out new chips in battle for data center business
summary: Intel Corp. announced a new line of Xeon Scalable Processor chips designed for data centers, aiming to compete with Advanced Micro Devices and other chip providers in the lucrative cloud computing market. These new chips offer enhanced support for next-generation computing applications like artificial intelligence and driverless cars, with Google Cloud Platform being the first data center to adopt them. The article highlights the competitive landscape, noting AMD's new data center processor and the growing trend of large internet companies designing their own hardware to push Intel on pricing.

title: Amazon’s Prime Day Proves to Be Biggest Shopping Day Ever
summary: Amazon's third annual Prime Day was its biggest shopping day ever, with sales surpassing Black Friday and Cyber Monday. The event, which included significant discounts on Echo devices, drove a substantial increase in new Prime members and sales, growing by more than 60% compared to the previous year. Amazon uses Prime Day to promote its membership and expand the reach of its Alexa platform, facing increasing competition from retailers like Walmart and Macy's.

title: Amazon Prime Day generates estimated $1 billion in sales
summary: Amazon's third annual Prime Day, a 30-hour sales event, generated an estimated $1 billion in revenue, making it the e-commerce giant's biggest sales day ever. Analysts from Cowen & Co. and JPMorgan Chase & Co. estimate this revenue, which was triple Amazon's average daily e-commerce revenue in 2016. The event saw "tens of millions" of Prime members making purchases, with the Echo Dot mini-speaker being the most popular item.

title: Software giant Adobe to build new facility, double Utah workforce
summary: Adobe Inc. announced plans to expand its Utah presence significantly by building a new $90 million facility and adding almost 1,300 employees at its Lehi campus. The expansion includes a 20-year tax incentive package from the Governor’s Office of Economic Development, totaling $25.8 million in tax breaks on projected new state wages of $2.3 billion. This move follows a trend of tech growth in Utah, including expansions by Amazon and Podium.

title: Netflix Expands in Hollywood
summary: Netflix has expanded its presence in Hollywood by leasing an additional 43,000 square feet at Sunset Bronson Studios from Hudson Pacific Properties Inc., adding to their existing 99,000 square feet. This deal demonstrates the high demand for state-of-the-art production facilities in Hollywood and highlights Hudson Pacific's success in securing long-term leases with top content creators like Netflix. The expansion is part of a broader revitalization of Hollywood as an entertainment production capital, driven by significant investments from Hudson Pacific and the convergence of tech and entertainment.

title: Kroger hires Aldi exec to run discounter Ruler Foods
summary: Kroger has hired Liz Ferneding, an Aldi veteran, to serve as president of its Ruler Foods discount division, an unusual move for the company that typically promotes from within. This appointment signals Kroger's intent to develop and expand the Ruler banner amidst increasing competition from retailers like Aldi and Lidl. The hire is seen as a strategic move to leverage Ferneding's expertise in discounters to help Kroger regain momentum after recent financial struggles.

title: How Much of Your Company’s Stock Is Too Much?
summary: This article discusses the risks of holding too much of one's company's stock in retirement plans, using Kroger Co. as a case study. The significant drop in Kroger's share price following Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods Market Inc. illustrates how quickly employees can lose a substantial portion of their savings due to company-specific events. The piece emphasizes that investing where one works is inherently riskier than it might seem.

title: Fined for Arriving Early? Wal-Mart Puts Its Suppliers on Notice
summary: Walmart is implementing stricter delivery rules for its suppliers, effective August, to improve product availability and add $1 billion to revenue. Suppliers of "fast-turning items" will face a 3% fine on the value of goods for late, missing, or early shipments if they fail to meet a 75% on-time, in-full delivery rate, with a target of 95% by February. This "On-Time, In-Full" (OTIF) program is a strategic move to boost efficiency and confront competition from Amazon.

Graphiq, founded as FindTheBest, specialized in organizing and connecting data to simplify online research, having previously developed tools for news publishers and an Alexa app. The acquisition brings Graphiq's data analysis technology and its employees into Amazon, strengthening Amazon's competitive position against other major tech companies in delivering quick answers to consumer queries.

title: Will Online Food Delivery Get “Amazoned”?
summary: Morgan Stanley research indicates that the online food delivery market is rapidly expanding, posing a significant disruption to the traditional restaurant industry, similar to how Amazon disrupted retail. Consumer demand is growing, with 40% of total restaurant sales, or $220 billion, potentially shifting to delivery by 2020. This trend will likely favor fast-food restaurants but could lead to cannibalization and profit-margin pressure for casual dining, while paradoxically having less impact on pizza delivery.

summary: The RealReal CEO Julie Wainwright stated in a video interview that the luxury consignment e-tailer is preparing to go public, aiming for an IPO rather than a sale. The company, which has raised $173 million, including a recent $50 million round, connects buyers and sellers of vetted luxury items and plans to open a brick-and-mortar store in New York City. Despite facing competitors, The RealReal distinguishes itself through its focus on luxury goods and its commission-based model.

title: A Foolish Take: Amazon.com makes most of its money from web services
summary: Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) generates the majority of its operating income, specifically three-quarters last year, from its cloud computing business, Amazon Web Services (AWS), rather than from its well-known retail operations. This high profitability from AWS, which brought in $12.2 billion in revenue with wide profit margins, allows Amazon to subsidize its retail prices, which generated only $1.1 billion in operating income from $124 billion in sales. The article highlights that Amazon developed AWS initially for internal needs before realizing its potential as a service to others, underscoring its strategic importance and profitability within the company.

title: Lenovo CEO vows to hit online sales target, or quit| Gulf Times
summary: Lenovo CEO Yang Yuanqing has publicly vowed to step down if he doesn't achieve a critical online sales goal of 80bn yuan ($12bn) within three years. He is betting big on artificial intelligence with a $1bn investment and aiming to transform the company’s sales online into an e-commerce juggernaut through JD.com Inc. While Lenovo faces challenges with its smartphone and data center businesses remaining in the red, Yang is exploring new growth avenues, including a potential tie-up with Japan’s Fujitsu for their PC businesses.

title: Campbell Soup Company rolls out its recipe for an e-commerce future
summary: Campbell Soup Company is embarking on an aggressive e-commerce strategy to achieve $300 million in online revenue within five years. This initiative includes investments in digital marketing, partnerships with companies like Amazon and The Sage Project, and a $10 million stake in meal kit start-up Chef'D. To lead this transformation, Campbell's has hired Shakeel Farooque as VP and Head of Digital and E-Commerce, signaling a significant shift for the 148-year-old CPG firm in response to a changing retail landscape.

title: Tech group sides with Apple in Qualcomm dispute
summary: A group representing major technology companies, including Alphabet Inc.'s Google, Amazon.com Inc., Microsoft Corp., and Facebook Inc., has aligned with Apple Inc. against Qualcomm Inc. in their legal dispute. The group urged regulators to reject Qualcomm's request to ban iPhone imports, arguing it would disrupt supply and harm consumers. This move comes amid a broader legal battle where Apple objects to Qualcomm's patent licensing model, and Qualcomm has accused Apple of withholding payments and infringing patents.

title: ‘We must be bold’: How Campbell Soup is adapting to food’s rapidly changing future
summary: Campbell Soup executives believe the company can adapt to the rapidly changing food industry by evolving its product mix and seizing e-commerce opportunities despite critics questioning its future. The company is aggressively investing in online businesses, acquiring natural and organic brands, and reformulating existing products to cater to evolving consumer demands for healthier, more transparent foods and new purchasing methods. Campbell aims to make "bold moves" and move quickly to capitalize on the growth of grocery e-commerce and consolidate its position in a dynamic retail environment.

title: Even Campbell Soup is taking a page from Amazon
summary: Campbell Soup Co. is strategically shifting towards e-commerce by hiring a former Amazon executive to lead its new e-commerce division. This move includes leveraging investments in meal-kit companies Chef'd and Habit, and building new distribution centers specifically for online orders. The company aims to differentiate itself in a changing retail landscape, mirroring Amazon's disruptive approach to revolutionize food delivery.

title: IPG Mediabrands launches MAGNA in India | Media4Growth
summary: IPG Mediabrands launched MAGNA in India, a centralized resource for Intelligence, Investment, and Innovation strategies for its agency teams and clients. The agency, which is the second-largest media agency network in India, will roll out MAGNA starting August 2017 with Hema Malik and Arun Sharma as joint heads. This initiative aims to provide competitive marketplace advantages through aggregated spending, advanced media buying, and industry-standard ad forecasts.

title: Your Roomba May Be Mapping Your Home, Collecting Data That Could Be Shared (Published 2017)
summary: High-end Roomba models collect spatial data to map users' homes, raising privacy concerns about how this data could be shared with companies like Amazon, Apple, or Google. While iRobot stated they have no plans to sell data and Reuters issued a correction regarding previous reports, the potential for targeted advertising based on home layouts and contents remains a sensitive issue in smart home data privacy. Digital rights groups warn that such data could allow advertisers to deduce income levels and even identify brands used by homeowners.

title: Amazon juggernaut sets its sights on its next victim: The middleman
summary: Amazon's growing Amazon Business platform, which recently surpassed $1 billion in sales, is increasingly threatening traditional "middleman" industrial distributors. Companies like W.W. Grainger (GWW) and Fastenal are facing pressure from Amazon's aggressive pricing, leading to analyst downgrades and profit concerns. While larger customers still value the expertise and service provided by traditional distributors, Amazon's continued expansion could significantly disrupt the $7 trillion business-to-business (B2B) market.

title: Smart Vacuum Cleaners Making Map Of Your Home — And Wants to Sell It
summary: iRobot, the company behind the Roomba vacuum cleaner, is reportedly planning to sell the home mapping data collected by its devices to third-party companies like Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. While this raises significant privacy concerns, proponents suggest the data could enhance the functionality of other smart home devices. iRobot CEO Colin Angle states that this would only happen with users' consent and could lead to a more integrated smart home ecosystem.

title: Why Amazon invested in this cancer-testing startup founded by a Google exec
summary: Amazon invested in the cancer-testing startup Grail primarily to secure a future customer for its Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud business. Grail's ambitious technology for early cancer detection requires massive data processing and storage, making it an ideal client for AWS. The investment also positions Amazon for future growth in the genomics and healthcare data storage market, especially considering Grail's expansion into Asia.

title: Buy iRobot Corporation (IRBT) Stock Because the Robot Revolution Is Here
summary: iRobot Corporation (IRBT) stock is performing well due to strong Q2 results, especially driven by Amazon Prime Day sales of its Roomba vacuum. The article argues that the ongoing consumer robot revolution, fueled by the smart home and IoT trends, makes IRBT an attractive long-term investment. iRobot's strong leadership in the consumer robot market and promising product pipeline suggest continued financial growth.

summary: Amazon.com Inc CEO Jeff Bezos has surpassed Bill Gates to become the world's richest person, with a fortune of $90.6 billion, primarily due to Amazon's rising stock. The company's shares jumped 1.6 percent, boosting Bezos's net worth ahead of Amazon's second-quarter earnings report, which analysts anticipate will show a 22 percent increase in sales to $37.2 billion. Bezos's wealth reflects Amazon's expansion into diverse markets, including Whole Foods, fashion, and enterprise computing.

title: The Simple Truth: Private Selection, other Kroger brands drive sales
summary: Kroger is leveraging its strong portfolio of house brands, including Simple Truth and Private Selection, to compete in a fierce grocery market against rivals like Walmart, Amazon, and Lidl. These private labels drive sales, offer both value and premium options to customers, and provide strategic advantages like cost control and product innovation. Kroger's house brands represent a significant portion of its total sales, with some brands achieving multi-billion dollar annual revenues.

title: Amazon’s Jeff Bezos becomes world’s richest, unseating Bill Gates
summary: Jeff Bezos, CEO of Amazon, has surpassed Bill Gates to become the world's richest person, with an estimated fortune of $90.6 billion. This rise is attributed to Amazon's significant stock jump and its aggressive expansion into various new markets beyond e-commerce. Meanwhile, Bill Gates, a prolific philanthropist, holds a net worth of $90.1 billion, having donated $31.1 billion to charity through 2016.

title: Jeff Bezos overtakes Bill Gates as world’s richest person
summary: Jeff Bezos, founder of Amazon.com Inc., surpassed Bill Gates as the world's richest person on July 27, 2017, due to a surge in Amazon's stock ahead of its earnings report. Bezos's net worth reached $90.9 billion, slightly above Gates's $90.7 billion. Investors were scrutinizing Amazon Prime subscriptions and the performance of its cloud-computing division, Amazon Web Services.

summary: Jeff Bezos, the founder and CEO of Amazon.com, has surpassed Bill Gates of Microsoft to become the world's richest person. His net worth reached over $90.5 billion due to Amazon's stock prices, making him the first multi-billionaire to overtake Gates in seven years. Bezos owns about 17 percent of Amazon and also has holdings in The Washington Post and Blue Origin.

title: i.am+ buys Wink, the smart home hub formerly owned by Flex and Quirky
summary: i.am+, the company owned by musician Will.i.am, has acquired Wink, a smart home hub and platform. Flex sold Wink for $38.7 million upfront and a $20 million commitment for future manufacturing, marking a significant increase from the $15 million Flex paid Quirky for it. The acquisition allows i.am+ to expand into the smart home category, while Wink users are assured that operations and user experience will remain unchanged.

title: The number of US renter households hits 50-year high
summary: The number of US renter households has reached its highest level since 1965, with the share of renter households increasing from 31.2% in 2006 to 36.6% in 2016. This trend is driven by post-recession economics, including foreclosures and millennials entering the job market, creating strong demand for rental properties. While urban centers remain popular, there's also significant growth in suburban rentals, with investors targeting single-family homes adapted for the rental market.

title: Best Buy will restructure Geek Squad, affecting 400 employees
summary: Best Buy is restructuring its Geek Squad service, eliminating 400 remote agent positions. The company intends to offer these employees similar roles within stores or for making house calls, aiming to transition them to new in-person capacities. This move affects 400 employees, reflecting a shift in how Geek Squad services are delivered.

title: Investors are betting on grocery real estate
summary: Investors are increasingly viewing grocery real estate as a favorable long-term growth opportunity, a trend that contrasts with the broader retail sector's shift away from physical stores due to rising online sales. Properties housing Walmart Neighborhood Market stores are particularly popular investments due to Walmart's perceived stability as a revenue generator and long-term occupant. The grocery industry is also considered relatively immune to economic downturns, as food purchases are non-discretionary, although the growing threat of online grocery spending remains a key risk for this investment strategy.
